notes: Section Crinitum is sister to section Androceras and includes S. lycocarpum; Crinitum representatives are actinomorphic and isantherous. notes: M. australasica is source-resolved as nonheterantherous/non-reciprocal enantiostylous, but direct animal-pollination eligibility remains unresolved. phylogenetic_basis: Marazzi et al. 2006 place section Psilorhegma within Senna; S. surattensis remains a source-resolved congeneric comparison but is not a valid heteranthery-absence control.
notes: Rejected after source audit. Luo et al. 2009 explicitly sampled S. surattensis among species with heteromorphic stamens and Table 1 codes its stamen differentiation as long and short. The androecium has little morphological differentiation and all 10 stamens are fertile and similar in size, but weak differentiation is not confirmed absence of heteranthery. A replacement nonheterantherous control must be selected under the frozen protocol.

phylogenetic_basis: Marazzi et al. 2006 provide the Senna phylogenetic framework; S. surattensis remains a source-matched congeneric comparison but is not a valid heteranthery-absence control.
notes: Rejected after source audit. Luo et al. 2009 explicitly include S. surattensis among heteromorphic-stamen taxa and distinguish long and short stamen sets. Its differentiation is weak relative to S. bicapsularis, but that makes it a low-differentiation heterantherous comparison rather than a source-secure nonheterantherous control. Replacement control required.

phylogenetic_basis: Chen et al. 2025 TAXON DOI 10.1002/tax.13349 recover Osbeckia chinensis plus O. nepalensis as the lineage sister to Melastoma; Flora of China describes Osbeckia stamens as isomorphic and equal or subequal.
notes: Selected before BALANCE predictor extraction. van der Pijl 1939 directly observed multiple hymenopterans visiting O. chinensis; bee-sized visitors landed on the stamen bundle and contacted the stigma with the abdomen. Flora of China records isomorphic equal/subequal stamens, excluding the case-defining heteranthery. Modern phylogenomics places the O. chinensis/O. nepalensis lineage sister to Melastoma. The same-tribe/sister-lineage match is adjudicated without claiming a species-level sister pair.
